name: Nauders Dreiländereck
kurzbeschreibung: The Dreiländerstein near Nauders marks the border point where Austria, Switzerland and Italy meet.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Nauders Three-Country Border (Dreiländereck) atop the storied Reschen Pass in the Tyrolean Oberland represents one of Central Europe's most intriguing geographical and historic crossroads. Here, at an elevation of 2,179 meters, the national frontiers of Austria (Tyrol), Italy (South Tyrol), and Switzerland (Graubünden/Engadine) intersect at a historic tripartite marker stone. Cradled within the soaring massifs of the Ötztaler Alps and the glaciated Ortler Group, the mountain pass looks back on millenia of transit along the ancient Roman Via Claudia Augusta. To defend this critical alpine gateway, the Habsburg Empire erected the colossal Fortress Nauders (Festung Nauders) between 1834 and 1840: preserved today as the only fully intact military road roadblock from the imperial Austrian era, the five-story stone fortress commands the defile directly above the highway. Today, the border nexus provides boundless hiking, world-class singletrack biking, and immersive historical discovery.

Route & Requirements

Exploration options at the Three-Country Border range from insightful heritage visits to high-alpine border crest loops. The signature hike to the Three-Country Stone (2,179 m) departs from the upper terminal of the Bergkastel gondola (2,200 m): following an exceptionally panoramic trail, walkers traverse open pastures and boulder-strewn ridges to reach the border crest, where a few strides span three distinct nations (walking time approx. 1.5 hours, moderate grade T2, requiring surefootedness on rocky paths). Culture seekers and families should not miss a guided interior tour of Fortress Nauders: behind multi-meter stone walls, engineered passages navigate cannon casemates, firing loopholes, and historic military barracks (1-hour tour, grade T1, thrilling for school-age youngsters; jackets recommended inside subterranean chambers). Sturdy trekking footwear and valid travel passports are mandatory. Leashed dogs are permitted on mountain trails.

Visit & Arrival

Public transit travelers take ÖBB mainline trains to Landeck-Zams railway station, transferring directly to regional VVT bus line 210 running up to Nauders in roughly 50 minutes. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Reschenpass) and follow highway B180 up through the Upper Inn Valley toward the Italian border. Fortress Nauders sits directly off the highway with visitor parking. Ample free parking is provided at the base terminal of the Bergkastelbahn. The cable car operates daily from early June through mid-October.

Tips

Take an iconic souvenir photo at the Three-Country Stone standing simultaneously with one foot in Switzerland, another in Italy, and your hand resting in Austria. Dine on the sun veranda of the Bergkastel Panorama Restaurant, enjoying traditional Kaiserschmarrn pancakes facing the glaciated 3,905-meter pyramid of Mount Ortler.
preis: Kostenlos frei zugänglich (Führung Festung Nauders ca. 9 €; Bergkastelbahn ca. 26 €)
